excerpt: Check whether a code change weakens your tests. A test can pass after it stops checking something useful. checkwash reads your Git diff and flags known patterns such as deleted assertions, skipped tests, relaxed expectations, and CI checks that stop failing. - assert total == 105.3 + assert total > 0 The new assertion accepts many incorrect totals. checkwash flags changes like this for review, including changes written by coding agents. Runs locally. No LLM. No network during analysis. Never executes your code. You need Python 3.11+, Git and pipx. Install the CLI, then run it from a Git repository: pipx install checkwash==0.13.2 checkwash demo # 8 tampering cases and 1 honest fix, offline checkwash check # your uncommitted changes checkwash check HEAD~1..HEAD # your last commit If the checkwash command is not found, or Windows blocks the checkwash.exe launcher, run python -m checkwash check from your repository with the Python that installed the package (find pipx's Python). Without pipx, the installation guide installs the package with pip in a virtual environment, and the single-file zipapp needs no installation. These examples use 0.13.2; the guide tracks the latest verified CLI download and Action pin. The 0.13.2 release guide describes the Python import fixes, CLI changes and measured Django scan times. - Branch review from merge base: checkwash check BASE...HEAD (BASE..HEAD compares the two snapshots directly) - Hands-on walkthrough: follow examples/invoice in a clone of this repository, with pytest installed, to watch a failing test, a one-line shortcut edit that makes it green without fixing the bug, and checkwash's block. Running check from a subdirectory analyses the whole repository from its Git root and notes that root on stderr (#416). For JSON/SARIF output and machine integration, see the embedding guide and stability contracts.
